original_text: Use a normal bank wire (SWIFT) from your Chinese bank, converting CNY to USD within China’s annual individual foreign-exchange quota of US$50,000 per person per calendar year. Within the quota you need only your ID — no tax penalty in China, just the bank’s FX spread and wire fee. Above the quota, you must document the legitimate source of the funds (for a foreigner working in China, after-tax salary with tax payment records can be remitted on top of the quota). Moving your own already-taxed money to the US is not a US taxable event — but you must still file US reports (FBAR if your foreign accounts aggregate over US$10,000; Form 8938/FATCA above higher thresholds; Form 3520 if the money is a gift over US$100,000 from a foreign person). Never use underground money changers or crypto P2P — both are illegal in China and carry fines of 30%–300% of the amount plus criminal risk.
